title: SLO-driven Scheduler Autotune Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the SLO-driven Scheduler Autotuner: a control loop that adjusts runtime scheduling parameters and kernel selection preferences to meet tenant and global SLOs while minimizing cost. It covers architecture, signals, tuning procedures, canary/rollout steps, observability dashboards, and triage steps for common failure modes.

Goals and scope:
- Primary goal: keep per-route and per-model latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) within target while maximizing throughput and minimizing per-token GPU cost.
- Secondary goals: avoid oscillation, preserve fairness across tenants, and provide deterministic rollback.
- Scope: inference request scheduler, kernel mapper hints, batching window, prefetching hints, and priority shaping. Not in scope: model parameter changes, quantization format changes, or hardware auto-scaling (handled by capacity-control).

Context and assumptions:
- Runtime exposes the following knobs: batch_max_tokens, batch_time_ms, kernel_hint (preferred kernel profile), kvcache_prefetch=true/false, priority_boost (integer), and graceful_preempt_timeout_ms.
- Telemetry: scheduler emits per-route aggregated metrics every 10s; per-request traces are sampled at 0.1% by default.
- SLOs can be defined at route, model, and tenant levels. Autotuner operates bottom-up: route -> model -> tenant.

Signals and telemetry (observable list):
- Latency.P50.route.<route> (ms)
- Latency.P95.route.<route> (ms)
- Latency.P99.route.<route> (ms)
- TailQueueDepth.route.<route> (requests)
- KernelExecutionTime.avg (ms) by kernel_hint
- BatchSize.mean and BatchSize.p95
- KVCacheHitRate.route.<route> (ratio)
- GPUUtilization.device (percent)
- SchedulingDecision.count.policy.<policy> (counter)
- AutotuneAction.events (counter with labels: action=scale_batch/time/kernel_hint)
- Cost.per_token.estimate (USD)
- ErrorRate.route.<route> (5xx + 4xx as separate series)

Key SLO examples (company defaults):
- Soft SLO: Latency.P95.route.* < 120ms
- Hard SLO: Latency.P99.route.* < 300ms
- Availability SLO: ErrorRate.route.* < 0.5% (rolling 1h)
- Cost target: per_token_cost.delta <= +20% from baseline for non-critical routes

Autotuner decision policy overview:
- Policy input: last 5m rolling metrics, traffic shape (sequence length histogram), GPU capacity, current batch stats, and recent autotune actions.
- Priority: preserve Hard SLO > Soft SLO > cost minimization.
- Action set (atomic): increase/decrease batch_time_ms by up to 20%, increase/decrease batch_max_tokens by up to 2x/0.5x, switch kernel_hint to compatible alternative, enable kvcache_prefetch on warm routes, apply priority_boost for short burst latency reduction.
- Cooldown: minimum 5 minutes between actions targeting the same route.

Control loop pseudo-algorithm (high level):
1. Aggregate metrics for each route for the last 5m.
2. If Latency.P99 > Hard SLO -> take emergency fallback action: reduce batch_time_ms by 50% and apply priority_boost=2.
3. Else if Latency.P95 > Soft SLO -> conservative action: reduce batch_time_ms by 20% or switch to lower-latency kernel_hint.
4. Else if Latency.P50 << SLO and GPUUtilization < 60% and Cost.per_token too high -> increase batch_time_ms up to 20% to improve cost efficiency.
5. Propose action -> run local simulation (see section "local simulation harness") -> score expected impact -> if score positive apply action with step and start cooldown.

Components and responsibilities:
- Scheduler Autotuner service (autotuner-svc): evaluates metrics, recommends actions, delegates to runtime-config API. Owner: serving-runtime/scheduling team.
- Runtime-config service: accepts config patches and enforces validation & safety. Owner: runtime-core.
- Telemetry bridge (telemetry-proxy): supplies metrics and sample traces to autotuner. Owner: telemetry-infra.
- Canary orchestrator: runs per-route canaries when enabled. Owner: rollout-planning team.

Config schema (example YAML):
---
policy_name: slo_latency_balancer_v1
routes:
  - id: \/v1\/generate
    hard_slo_ms: 300
    soft_slo_ms: 120
    cost_sensitivity: low
    allowed_kernels: ["opt-low-latency", "opt-balanced"]
  - id: \/v1\/embed
    hard_slo_ms: 400
    soft_slo_ms: 200
    cost_sensitivity: medium
global:
  cooldown_minutes: 5
  max_concurrent_actions: 2
  emergency_action:
    reduce_batch_time_pct: 50
    priority_boost: 2
---

CLI examples and debug commands:
- Enable autotuner for a policy: rdwctl runtime autotune apply --policy slo_latency_balancer_v1 --env prod
- Disable autotuner: rdwctl runtime autotune disable --policy slo_latency_balancer_v1 --env prod
- Force an emergency rollback: rdwctl runtime config rollback --policy slo_latency_balancer_v1 --to-revision 42
- Query recent actions: curl -sS "https:\/\/runtime-api.internal.autotune\/actions?route=\/v1\/generate" | jq

Local simulation harness (developer workflow):
1. Pull 10m of production metric slices (export via telemetry-proxy) for the route under test.
2. Run autotuner-sim --policy policy.yaml --metrics sample.json --simulate-horizon 10m --output scoring.json
3. Review scoring.json for expected p50/p95/p99 and cost delta.

Canary & rollout plan (recommended):
1. Dry-run: schedule autotuner in dry-run mode for 30 minutes to collect proposed actions without applying them. Validate proposed actions against canary rules.
2. Canary (2% traffic): apply only kernel_hint and batch_time_ms conservative adjustments. Observe for 1h.
3. Canary (10% traffic): apply full action set but limit to max_concurrent_actions=1. Observe 2h.
4. Ramp to 50% traffic and then 100% if metrics are stable and no hard SLO violations.

Deployment success criteria (example):
- No Hard SLO violations during 4h post-rollout.
- AutotuneAction.events with action=reduce_batch_time count <= 0.1% of requests.
- Per-token cost changes within policy-defined limits.

Roll forward / rollback triggers:
Roll back immediately if any of the following occur within the post-rollout observation window:
- Any route hits Hard SLO for > 5m sustained.
- ErrorRate increases by > 0.3 percentage points versus baseline.
- Unexplained GPU saturation (utilization > 95% with no matching throughput increase).

Debugging checklist (fast triage):
1. Check autotuner action logs: rdwctl runtime autotune actions --recent 50 --route \/v1\/generate
2. Inspect last-applied runtime-config revision and diffs.
3. Correlate with sampled request traces (trace-id from action log).
4. If kernel_hint switch coincided with regression, revert kernel_hint before other actions.
5. If batch_time_ms reductions created instability, scale back to previous revision and increase cooldown.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Oscillation (autotuner bounces knobs repeatedly): raise cooldown_minutes, increase hysteresis thresholds, add action dampening (apply fractional steps).
- Cold-route regression: enable kvcache_prefetch only after route warmup (threshold: 100 successful inferences within last 10m).
- Unhandled kernel incompatibility: autotuner must validate allowed_kernels list; runtime-config rejects incompatible kernel_hint by returning 422. Fallback action: revert kernel_hint and mark route for manual review.

Runbook: emergency response (p99 breach detected):
1. Acknowledge alert on #runtime-ops and tag oncall.
2. Run rdwctl runtime autotune emergency --policy <policy> --route <route> (this applies emergency_action).
3. Monitor p99, GPUUtilization, and ErrorRate for 15 minutes.
4. If still exceeding Hard SLO after emergency action, scale to reserved capacity pool (see oncall runbook: eng-sre/capacity-planning).
5. Open incident with severity=SLO-Breach and include autotuner action timeline and traces.

Observability & dashboards (must-have panels):
- Per-route SLO panel: p50/p95/p99 with thresholds overlaid.
- Autotune Actions timeline: actions annotated on latency charts.
- BatchSize distribution heatmap and queue depth.
- Kernel execution time by hint and by model version.
- Cost per token trend vs baseline.
- Action-to-latency correlation scatter (expected delta).

Prometheus example queries (appendix):
- p99 for route: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket{route=\"\/v1\/generate\"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- KVCache hit rate: sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total{route=\"\/v1\/generate\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_requests_total{route=\"\/v1\/generate\"}[5m]))
- Autotune actions: sum(rate(autotune_actions_total[5m])) by (action, route)

Appendix: example runtime-config patch (JSON):
{
  "route": "\/v1\/generate",
  "changes": {
    "batch_time_ms": 12,
    "kernel_hint": "opt-low-latency",
    "priority_boost": 1
  },
  "metadata": {
    "trigger": "autotuner",
    "policy": "slo_latency_balancer_v1"
  }
}

- Primary contacts: Maya Chen (author), Jordan Lee (scheduler lead).
- Escalation: Eng SRE -> Runtime Core -> CTO on persistent unresolved SLO breach.

Notes and future work:
- Planned: add reinforcement-learning–based estimator for longer-horizon traffic patterns; until validated this remains a disabled experimental branch.
- Planned: per-tenant cost-aware objectives to allow pay-for-performance priorities.
